sections.content: Who I am. I am a designer passionate about combining technology, human-centered thinking, and creative problem-solving to shape meaningful, user-focused solutions. I value optimism and open-mindedness, believing these traits fuel creativity, collaboration, and motivation. My strength lies in connecting people and disciplines, facilitating inclusive, stakeholder-driven processes where diverse perspectives lead to better outcomes \cite{springer1994}. In team settings, I naturally take on a coordinating role, ensuring all voices and ideas are heard and shared. My Bachelor's in Creative Technology at the University of Twente provided a foundation bridging hardware, software, and user needs. Foundation. For example: designing electronic circuits, iterative prototyping \ref{data-physicalization-museum}, or a low-poly game from scratch (\ref{interactive-media}), translating abstract ideas into functional code and custom assets.

Beyond academia, co-founding a startup (\ref{exomembra}) immersed me in the end-to-end design processes, from conceptualizing wearable art to building a responsive web shop. Collaborating directly with customers to align designs with their needs taught a balance between creativity and practicality. Similarly, designing an information system (\ref{student-management}) again revealed the value of including stakeholders in the design, they showed multiple elements they valued I did not expect, reinforcing my commitment to inclusive, iterative processes. These projects showed the importance of involving stakeholders and users in the design to ensure adoption and real-world relevance.

How I work. In my design approach, flexibility is key. I adapt methodologies to fit each project (\ref{wordbond}, \ref{fmp-hcd}, \ref{tactone}), drawing from diverse frameworks. In group projects, I prioritize a clear and structured approach to ensure transparency and accountability. Personal projects follow a more spontaneous path driven by curiosity and exploration, allowing me to experiment freely and learn by doing.

What drives me. What drives me in my work is a focus on solving problems. Over time, I've grown more confident in my ability to tackle challenges by breaking them down and applying my skillset. I used to see personal motivation as the main factor for completing projects, and also my biggest pitfall, since it can be an unstable factor for specializing. But, during the master, I noticed my motivation shift to the process itself and the satisfaction of finding solutions. I'm still navigating the balance between specialization and generalization, as I'm driven both by a desire to master specific skills and by the excitement of connecting diverse ideas across fields. Where I struggle. While I thrive in collaborative environments, I sometimes struggle when others show a lack of initiative, which can lead me to take over tasks to maintain momentum. I'm aware this tendency could hinder team dynamics, and I aim to improve my ability to navigate these situations, as it will likely also be part of future professional settings. In summary, I am a designer dedicated to leveraging technology thoughtfully and responsibly, balancing creativity, technical skills, and human-centered design to craft solutions that make a meaningful impact.
